tasks.short: Design, run and assess search marketing experiments to improve qualified traffic and conversions.

steps.what: Collect search, conversion and landing-page performance from {ADS}, {BI} and {CMS}.
Reconcile attribution, traffic exclusions and baseline metrics in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Write a test hypothesis, primary metric, allocation, stopping rule and guardrails.
Prepare copy and page variants against the experiment plan.

loop.input: Experiment plan, approved claims, brand guidelines and existing page copy.
loop.output: Named copy variants linked to their hypothesis and supporting claims.
loop.check: Validate lengths, links and claim references; strategist checks meaning and experimental isolation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per requested variant; unresolved checks return to the strategist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but materially different wording requires language generation.

steps.what: Review test validity, spend exposure and variants; approve or request changes.
Configure and launch approved variants through {ADS} or the {CMS}.
Calculate effects, uncertainty and guardrail breaches in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Decide whether to adopt, reject or extend the tested change.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles {ADS}, {CMS} and {BI} data and calculates results against a versioned experiment plan. A bounded drafting loop prepares variants in {DOCS}; configured experiment tools publish only the version covered by the marketing manager's approval. A {BI} dashboard exposes measurement failures and uncertainty, leaving hypothesis selection and adoption recommendations with the strategist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data joins, attribution differences and repeated test setup made small experiments costly. Sound experimental design still required expertise.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing experiment settings handle allocation where supported. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building connectors, validation and reusable statistical calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Low traffic, delayed conversions and overlapping campaigns can prevent useful conclusions. Organic search tests need suitable page cohorts and controls; visitor-level randomisation is not always valid.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a commercially meaningful hypothesis and recognise when a measured lift reflects attribution or audience changes.

ambition.what: A weekly landing-page experiment allocation decision for sufficiently trafficked pages.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling results to selecting experiments and investigating surprising effects. The strategist can gain authority to extend or stop tests within approved spend and guardrails; wider rollout remains with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Design landing-page variants that isolate one user-experience hypothesis.
reach.learn: Accessible interaction design, component constraints and experimental contamination.

evidence.claim: Data reconciliation, experiment calculations and rule-based alerts can be implemented deterministically; effectiveness depends on measurement quality.
The digest provides no direct documented case establishing search experiment automation or its time savings.

assumptions: Today's process combines native system screens, spreadsheet analysis and written test plans.
Native experiment configuration is available for the selected channel; custom allocation would require a different estimate.
Build ranges are planning estimates for a limited rollout, not measured productivity claims.
Access work includes checking GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and national consultation rules. Employee-level monitoring is outside scope.
Testing and rollout estimates exclude calendar time needed to accumulate experiment traffic.
unknowns: Which experiment features and data interfaces are licensed?
Are conversion definitions, consent signals and attribution windows consistent?
Which pages have enough traffic for a useful test?
What spend and stopping decisions may the strategist make?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the proposed implementation?
research_questions: Which experimental design best limits interference between organic search page cohorts?
Which statistical stopping method suits delayed conversions and repeated monitoring?
new_work: Review reconciliation exceptions and tracking failures.
Maintain metric definitions, exclusions and calculation tests.
Review generated variants and their claim references.
Keep approvals tied to exact plan and variant versions.

tasks.short: Prepare, launch and monitor coordinated online campaigns across selected paid, partner, email and social channels.

steps.what: Translate the approved proposal into channel objectives, audiences, budgets and dates.
Coordinate affiliate or sponsorship availability, deliverables and proposed terms through {EMAIL}.
Draft channel copy and assemble approved visual assets.

loop.input: Channel plan, approved claims, brand guidelines and approved asset library.
loop.output: Channel-specific copy with claim references and selected asset identifiers.
loop.check: Validate format limits, links and asset permissions; strategist checks claims, tone and audience fit.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per requested asset; unresolved items return to the strategist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed templates handle assembly, but adapting a message to several channel contexts requires language work.

steps.what: Build draft placements, messages and landing pages in the selected channel systems.
Check destinations, tracking, audience permissions, suppression rules and campaign previews.
Approve spend, claims, audience use and any partner commitments.
Release the approved campaign and confirm authorised partner placements.
Review delivery, spend and conversion results; flag required corrections.

tasks.design: A campaign record in {PROJECT} holds the channel plan, asset versions, checks and approval; configured templates populate drafts in {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {SOCIAL} and {CMS}. A bounded loop drafts copy from approved material, while deterministic checks validate destinations, tracking and documented audience permissions. The release workflow consumes the version-specific approval, and a {BI} dashboard highlights delivery and spend exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each channel had its own setup, identifiers and approval trail. Coordination and repeated asset entry made a shared release process expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and scheduling cover much of execution. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining validation and channel connectors cheaper to build; bounded drafting reduces copy preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Partner negotiations, creative judgement and inconsistent channel capabilities remain. GDPR, national electronic marketing rules and EU AI Act applicability require context-specific checks; a permission flag alone does not establish lawful audience use.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise poor audience fit, misleading promises and partner arrangements that could damage trust.

ambition.what: A repeatable regional campaign package for smaller local sales teams.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time entering campaigns and more time adjusting channel choices and reviewing exceptions. They can gain authority to pause delivery within approved guardrails; new spend, audience uses and partner commitments retain their existing approvers.

reach.task: Coordinate channel budgets and partner placement schedules.
reach.learn: Media buying terms, incremental reach and budget pacing.

reach.task: Prepare reusable visual assets for channel formats.
reach.learn: Asset specifications, visual hierarchy and usage rights.

evidence.claim: Shopify Sidekick generates product descriptions. This supports the feasibility of bounded copy drafting, not end-to-end campaign execution.
Campaign templates, scheduling, suppression checks and performance dashboards can use configuration and deterministic integrations.

assumptions: The decomposition represents a campaign using several selected channels; partner coordination is absent when no partner channel is used.
Draft creation does not send messages, activate spend or transfer customer lists to new recipients.
Partner coordination gathers proposed terms; commitments take effect only after campaign approval.
The marketing manager has the required delegated authority and obtains specialist review when needed.
Build ranges cover one campaign family and supported interfaces. Advertising spend and partner fees are excluded from run cost.
Access work includes privacy review and checking national consultation requirements; employee-level performance monitoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Which channels permit draft creation and controlled release through available interfaces?
Who may approve partner commitments and customer audience transfers?
Where are audience permissions, objections and suppression records maintained?
Which native templates and scheduling features are already configured?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the implementation?
research_questions: Which channel interfaces preserve preview, approval and release as separate operations?
Which measurement approach best estimates incremental results across overlapping channels?
new_work: Review generated copy, claims and visual selections.
Maintain channel templates and interface mappings.
Resolve permission, tracking and delivery exceptions.
Revalidate approval whenever assets, recipients, spend or partner terms change.

tasks.short: Combine search, commerce, competitor and public-topic signals into evidence-backed market opportunities.

steps.what: Export metrics from {ADS}, {ECOMMERCE}, {SOCIAL} and search analytics tools in {OTHER}.
Collect dated news and competitor pages using web research tools in {OTHER}.
Align dates, markets, currencies and query categories in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Interpret query intent and public sources alongside measured trends.

loop.input: Dated source bundle, query text, calculated trends and research scope.
loop.output: Intent categories and candidate explanations with source references and uncertainty.
loop.check: Require resolvable references and supporting passages; verify every quantity against the trend dataset.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair over the fixed bundle; unsupported claims are removed or queued.
loop.why_not_simpler: Numeric trend detection is deterministic, but intent and narrative context depend on free text.

steps.what: Rank opportunities against customer relevance, commercial fit and evidence strength.
Email a recurring market digest with attached charts to stakeholders.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collect authorised metrics from {ADS}, {ECOMMERCE}, {SOCIAL} and research tools in {OTHER}, retaining dates and provenance. Deterministic calculations feed a {BI} dashboard, while a bounded loop drafts source-linked intent analysis in {DOCS} for strategist review. Stakeholders use the shared dashboard and opportunity brief, eliminating the recurring attachment digest.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research sources used different definitions and export formats. Reading public material and maintaining traceable notes added recurring effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable connectors and calculation rules automate collection and comparison. Bounded language processing can organise a fixed source bundle without autonomous browsing.
tasks.still_hard: Competitor performance is usually inferred from incomplete observations. Sampling, seasonality, source coverage and changing platform definitions can create false trends.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a commercially useful change in intent from publicity, measurement noise or a competitor's temporary promotion.

ambition.what: A weekly emerging-intent brief for product assortment planning.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting exports to investigating signals and discussing opportunities. The strategist can publish evidence-ranked research within an agreed scope; campaign investment rights do not automatically change.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Validate whether an observed trend reflects a durable customer need.
reach.learn: Sampling limitations, triangulation and qualitative research design.

reach.task: Evaluate assortment gaps against emerging search intent.
reach.learn: Stock constraints, product margins and category economics.

evidence.claim: Scheduled collection, normalisation and trend calculations are deterministic; free-text intent analysis can use a bounded model loop.
A documented report containing nonexistent citations illustrates why generated research needs source verification; it does not establish marketing automation performance.

assumptions: Collection uses a finite source register and authorised feeds, interfaces or exports.
The initial service covers selected markets and languages rather than unrestricted web discovery.
Public competitor observations are labelled as estimates, not internal competitor results.
GDPR applies when query or audience data can identify people; aggregated research is preferred.
Build ranges include source-access review and checking national consultation requirements. Additional licensing costs depend on source contracts.
unknowns: Which research sources are licensed for automated retrieval and storage?
Which markets, languages and competitors are in scope?
Do available query exports contain personal data?
Which historical definitions changed across the comparison period?
Will stakeholders replace attachment digests with the shared research view?
Do national rules require employee consultation for this implementation?
research_questions: Which sources provide sufficiently independent evidence to corroborate search-demand changes?
How can multilingual intent categories be validated without hiding local differences?
new_work: Maintain the source register, retrieval permissions and source mappings.
Review missing data and definition changes.
Check intent classifications, citations and unsupported explanations.
Retire weak signals and compare prior opportunity calls with later outcomes.

tasks.short: Develop and present evidence-backed campaign proposals for marketing investment decisions.

steps.what: Gather objectives, prior results, market opportunities and delivery constraints.
Estimate channel costs, conversion ranges and commercial scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss campaign concepts and choose a recommended audience, offer and channel mix.
Write the proposal with alternatives, economics, evidence, risks and a measurement plan.

loop.input: Selected concept, calculated scenarios, evidence pack and proposal template.
loop.output: A campaign proposal with referenced claims, alternatives and explicit assumptions.
loop.check: Validate figures against scenario outputs and references against the evidence pack; strategist reviews the argument.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence remains marked as a gap and blocks unsupported claims.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but explaining the campaign's specific rationale requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Present the recommendation, answer challenges and negotiate scope.
Approve, reject or return the proposal within delegated investment authority.
Record the decision and hand approved scope to campaign delivery.

tasks.design: A proposal workspace in {PROJECT} assembles approved evidence from {BI} and {DOCS}, while a deterministic calculator produces scenarios from explicit assumptions. A bounded drafting loop fills the proposal in {DOCS}; the strategist chooses the concept and presents the recommendation. The marketing manager records the investment decision, and a configured workflow hands only approved scope to delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence gathering, scenario updates and repeated proposal writing consumed preparation time. Agreement on priorities and investment could not be reduced to a template.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable scenario calculators and evidence retrieval remove repeated assembly. Bounded drafting can turn a selected concept and verified numbers into a reviewable proposal.
tasks.still_hard: Forecasts depend on assumptions, channel overlap and delivery capacity. Executive persuasion and resolving conflicting objectives remain human work, so near-total automation is unlikely.
tasks.human_edge: Make an argument that reflects commercial priorities, defend its assumptions and change the recommendation when challenged.

ambition.what: A monthly comparison of a smaller pilot against the full campaign investment.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less of the week assembling proposals and more time testing assumptions with stakeholders. They can gain authority to recommend staged investment and stop criteria; final investment approval stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Compare campaign investments across competing commercial priorities.
reach.learn: Contribution economics, portfolio trade-offs and investment governance.

reach.task: Develop a campaign narrative from a commercial brief.
reach.learn: Audience framing, narrative structure and evidence-based persuasion.

evidence.claim: Scenario calculations and evidence-pack assembly can be deterministic; drafting can use a bounded loop over approved inputs.
The supplied digest does not document automated campaign proposal approval or establish that executive persuasion can be automated.

assumptions: Objectives, past results and approved assumptions exist in accessible records.
A proposal decision does not itself publish a campaign, transfer audience data or activate spend.
Rejected and returned proposals produce a decision record but no approved campaign proposal.
Build ranges cover one proposal template and scenario model; they are planning estimates.
Access work includes confidentiality, GDPR and EU AI Act applicability checks, plus national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Which commercial outcomes and cost assumptions govern investment decisions?
Who holds approval authority at each investment level?
Which proposal sections require specialist review?
How complete and comparable are historical campaign results?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the implementation?
research_questions: Which scenario presentation best communicates uncertainty without implying forecast precision?
How should staged campaign proposals account for learning value as well as immediate return?
new_work: Maintain scenario formulas, assumptions and proposal templates.
Review generated claims, references and the recommendation's logic.
Record approval scope and conditions precisely.
Compare forecasts with outcomes and update planning assumptions.

role.altitude: The role shifts from repeated data assembly and channel setup toward experiment design, market interpretation and investment recommendations. Useful new rights are bounded test stopping, campaign pausing and publishing scoped research; broader spending and publication decisions remain explicitly delegated.
reach: Help Web and Digital Interface Designers build measurable landing-page improvements.
Help Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists validate emerging customer needs.
Help Marketing Managers compare staged campaign investments.
Help Online Merchants connect search intent with assortment decisions.
skills_to_grow: Experimental design, uncertainty and causal inference.
Attribution, consent-aware measurement and data quality.
Source verification and multilingual intent analysis.
Accessible landing-page design and persuasive commercial writing.
role.ambitious_version: Run a shared search opportunity and experimentation service that turns verified demand signals into staged campaign proposals and measurable landing-page tests for central and regional teams.
